AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to the placing of a lien for unpaid property taxes against the proceeds of a fire insurance policy on any real property located within a municipality
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3691

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the general municipal law, in
relation to the placing of a lien for unpaid property taxes against
the proceeds of a fire insurance policy on any real property located
within a municipality

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To expand the definition of real property under the general municipal
law to include one and two family residential structures such that
municipalities may impose a tax lien upon an owner's fire insurance
policy in the event that the owner does not remedy damage to their
property.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Amends paragraph (e) of subdivision 1 of section 22 of the
general municipal law, as added by chapter 569 of the laws of 1978, to
include one and two family structures in the definition of real
property.

Section 2. This act shall take effect immediately

 JUSTIFICATION :

Current state law allows a municipality to impose a lien against the
fire insurance policy of a real property owner in the event that the
owner does not remedy damage to their property caused by a fire.
Presently, this law applies to residential, commercial, and industrial
properties, but excludes one and two family residences. This bill
would amend the general municipal law to hold all property-owners
accountable for the condition of their real property.

In 2005, a fire in the City of Albany's first ward damaged a block of
several houses. While other property owners made an effort to secure
their structures, one homeowner chose not to do so. The result was
water damage and mold to the home of his neighbor. This bill seeks to
give municipal governments a mechanism to ensure that all property
owners affected by a fire make best efforts to secure their property
and protect surrounding structures. By placing a lien against fire
insurance proceeds paid to the owner of a single or two-family
residence when the owner refuses to remedy fire damage, local
governments will be able to put an end to such situations and ensure
the safety of all their property owners.

Additionally, this bill will ensure that property owners cannot simply
collect an insurance settlement and abandon their property. This will
reduce instances of vacant structures and improve quality of life for
all members of the community.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-16 A.9588

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
